rows.title: use Contextmanagers to handle StopIteration in generators

outcomes.text: The new @contextmanager decorator requires an import. Add `from contextlib import contextmanager` at the top of the file; otherwise this module will fail to import.

`_runtest_for` is still annotated as `Generator[None]` but is now used as a context manager. Update the return type hint to `Iterator[None]` or `ContextManager[None]` to reflect its actual usage and avoid type‑checking warnings.

The wrapper hooks (`pytest_runtest_setup`, `pytest_runtest_call`, `pytest_runtest_teardown`) now use `with self._runtest_for(...): yield`. This changes the semantics from a generator to a context manager and may break pytest's expectation that these hooks return a generator. Verify that the hook wrapper protocol still works with this pattern; otherwise revert to `yield from` and handle StopIteration inside `_runtest_for`.

rows.title: terminal: notify terminal emulator about test session progress

outcomes.text: The new `TerminalProgressPlugin` uses `Literal`, `Session` and `TerminalReporter` types but they are not imported. Add the appropriate imports from `typing` and `pytest` modules.

`config.pluginmanager.register(plugin, "terminalprogress")` registers a plugin that may interfere with existing plugins that also hook `pytest_runtest_logreport`. Ensure the plugin is registered with `tryfirst=True` to avoid ordering issues.
The property `_is_last_item` now uses `self.reported_progress`. This property is private; consider keeping the original private attribute name for consistency with other internal checks.
`write_raw` duplicates the Unicode‑encode error handling logic already present in `write`. Consider extracting the error‑handling block into a shared helper to avoid code duplication.
`write_raw` does not apply markup handling. Calls to `write_raw` from the progress plugin will bypass any markup processing, which is intended, but document this behavior in the method docstring.
The progress percentage calculation uses integer division which may truncate values. Consider using `round` for a more accurate display, e.g. `round(self.reported_progress * 100 / collected)`.

rows.title: don't crash if exceptiongroup has only hidden tb frames

outcomes.text: The parametrization order (`tbstyle` then `group`) does not match the fixture signature order; pytest will pass `tbstyle` as the first argument and `group` as the second, which is fine, but the `ids` tuple refers to the second parameter only. Consider adding an explicit `ids` for `tbstyle` or reordering parameters for clarity.

When `group` is True the test raises an `ExceptionGroup` containing a `ValueError`. The assertion `result.stdout.fnmatch_lines(["*ValueError: bar"])` will still match, but the output also includes the `ExceptionGroup` header. It may be clearer to assert both the `ExceptionGroup` line and the inner `ValueError` line to avoid false positives.

The new `extraline` message is added only when `traceback` is falsy. However, the crash being fixed occurs when all frames are hidden but `traceback` is non‑empty. Consider also emitting the message when `traceback` exists but every entry is hidden, to ensure the user sees the guidance in that scenario.
